subject: arts-music
lesson_title: Unit assessment: advanced performance, direction, and production
standards: Michigan Arts Education Standards: Theatre — Performing
essential_question: What does it take to lead other people toward a shared interpretation?
learning_objectives: Demonstrate current mastery across advanced performance, direction, and production, showing process or evidence for each response.
Communicate understanding of advanced performance, direction, and production using subject-appropriate evidence or representation.
Check, revise, or improve the work on advanced performance, direction, and production against the stated success criteria.
lesson_success_criteria: The learner completes the central task on advanced performance, direction, and production.
The learner supplies evidence, reasoning, a model, or a documented process rather than an unsupported answer.
The learner checks or revises the work and can name a next step.
materials: script, score, or devised material — public-domain or original only
private rehearsal space; no recording equipment is required at any point

Household-accessible route: pencil or pen and scrap paper are enough. For sound or performance work, tap, clap, use spoken syllables, move a finger, or notate silently. Specialized art materials, instruments, paid software, cameras, microphones, and recording devices are optional and never affect credit.
task_brief: Day 11 of "Advanced Performance, Direction, and Production" (unit 4, grade 11) is an unit assessment on advanced performance, direction, and production. It is one step inside the unit — not the whole unit project — and takes about 45–75 minutes. The unit is working toward: Lead or execute an advanced performance or production element in a chosen private or shared format, with a rehearsal, direction, and feedback record. Today's work contributes to that by handling advanced performance, direction, and production at the unit assessment stage, against the unit's wider topics of advanced interpretation and stylistic fluency, directing and rehearsal leadership, technical design lighting sound and staging, and collaborative production planning. This session produces graded evidence of record and must be completed independently.
primary_task: Complete the unit assessment task for advanced performance, direction, and production independently and under the unit's stated conditions. Produce the required piece or analysis, show the process or reasoning behind it, and check it against the stated criteria before submitting. Include your own judgement: what you intended, what the work actually achieves, and where the gap is. Everything submitted must be your own authorship. Presentation stays private or written; no public performance, camera, voice recording, or photograph is required to complete or pass this task. Anchor today's work inside its unit: this session's evidence is about advanced performance, direction, and production, and it belongs to "Advanced Performance, Direction, and Production", which also covers separate topics such as advanced interpretation and stylistic fluency. Close out with this check before you stop: Identify the item you are least confident about and say what would resolve it. At grade 11 the bar is independent work with sustained self-direction: you set the constraint, defend it, and revise on the evidence of your own checks rather than on being told to.

presentation_and_privacy.presentation_options: You choose the audience. Keeping the work entirely to yourself, showing it to one parent or trusted adult, or submitting it as a file with no one watching are all full-credit options. No public performance, exhibition, class presentation, live audience, photograph, camera, or voice recording is required at any point in this task, and choosing the most private option never lowers the score.
presentation_and_privacy.text_or_no_audio_alternative: A written alternative is always available and scores the same. Instead of performing, speaking, or recording, you may submit a written description of what you made or would make, a notated or diagrammed version, a labelled plan, or a written analysis covering the same criteria. Nothing in this task requires a working microphone, camera, or the ability to perform aloud.

copyright_and_authorship: The graded submission must be your own authorship. A parent, tutor, or AI tool may explain an idea, demonstrate a technique, or give feedback on a draft, but must not produce, write, debug, or make any part of the work that is scored. Any material you did not create yourself must be in the public domain, openly licensed, or used as a short cited excerpt for study — reproduce no more than the point requires, credit the maker and the source, and never copy full lyrics, a complete score, or a whole image and present it as your own.
accessibility_options: Provide readable text plus optional audio or read-aloud support; no voice feature is required.
Chunk directions into one action at a time and show a worked example or model.
Offer reduced-copying, extended-time, hidden-timer, movement-break, and low-distraction options.
Use captions, alt text, high-contrast print, keyboard access, and text-only fallbacks for media.
For any multi-session project, supply a written milestone plan, checkpoint dates, and a task breakdown, so executive-function load is not silently part of what is being assessed.

Adjust quantity, pacing, representation, or response mode while holding the target constant. Where the target names a specific skill, change how it is evidenced rather than substituting a different skill.

Accept typed, handwritten, spoken, drawn, notated, constructed, or demonstrated responses. Where performance is the target, a private demonstration to one trusted adult carries the same weight as any audience, and requires no recording.
Provide adaptive instruments and grips, enlarged or braille notation, seated and standing studio access, low-odour and low-dust material substitutes, and hearing protection on request.

Where documentation quality is itself the target, document the artwork alone with no person in frame, or have an adult verify the physical work directly. Neither route requires an image of the learner, and both preserve the documentation target rather than replacing it.
task_accessibility_provisions: Where performance is the target, a private demonstration to one trusted adult carries exactly the same weight as any audience, and requires no recording. A written or notated account of the intended performance is a full substitute.

This work spans sessions, so supply a written milestone plan, explicit checkpoint dates, and a task breakdown. Executive-function load — sequencing, holding the plan in mind, remembering where the work stopped — must not become a silent part of what is being assessed.
Breaks, extended time, a hidden timer, reduced copying, and a low-distraction setting are available on request and never reduce the score.
safety_and_privacy_rules: Allow a pause, break, or alternate response mode without treating it as failure.
Protect hearing, ventilation, tool safety, cultural context, and respectful representation.
Public performance is never required. A private, low-audience, or written-and-scored alternative always carries the same academic target.
No recording of the learner’s voice, no photograph, and no video is ever required; documentation may be written, notated, sketched, or adult-verified instead.
Use only original, public-domain, licensed, or family-approved works. Do not reproduce full copyrighted lyrics, sheet music, or other protected works without documented rights.
The tutor may explain technique, ask diagnostic questions, and critique work, but never silently completes graded creative work.

media.suggestion: Optional diagram, score excerpt, worked example, source image, demonstration, or short clip supporting advanced performance, direction, and production.
media.fallback: Provide the same information as readable steps, alt text, transcript, tactile or concrete model, or adult demonstration.

remediation: Reteaching for advanced performance, direction, and production follows the signal actually observed, not a fixed script. If the signal is "prerequisite gap": Return to the smallest prerequisite needed for advanced performance, direction, and production, model it in a concrete or text-only representation, then retry one fresh item. If the signal is "procedure without understanding": Ask the learner to explain or represent why the approach to advanced performance, direction, and production works before continuing. If the signal is "correct but low confidence": Confirm the reasoning specifically, offer one varied example of advanced performance, direction, and production, and avoid unnecessary remediation. If the signal is "repeated error pattern": Name the observable pattern neutrally, contrast it with a worked example, and schedule a short same-day or next-session review. If the signal is "requests the answer to graded work": Explain the concept, ask a diagnostic question, or help isolate the defect. Do not supply the graded artifact, solution code, or finished creative work. If the signal is "mastery evidence": Require accurate independent application plus explanation on a later or different occasion before marking advanced performance, direction, and production mastered. Re-check with one fresh item of the same kind before moving on, and record which signal was seen so the pattern is visible across the unit rather than treated as a one-off.
extension: Apply advanced performance, direction, and production under a new constraint, compare two approaches or perspectives, or explain the idea to someone else using an original example. Treat this as optional depth on advanced performance, direction, and production rather than extra volume: one harder case done well beats three more of the same. Extension work stays private by default and uses only original, public-domain, or properly cited material. Extension work is never required to reach mastery and must not be assigned as a penalty.
